features.title: Cancelled region selection is a silent no-op
features.trigger: Cancelling the interactive region/window selection with Esc (screenshot.rs:12, 34), or leaving no file behind after the selection.
features.context: Interactive (Region) mode in practice; the no-file check at screenshot.rs:62-63 runs in both modes.
features.result: No screenshot is saved and no error or message is shown; the capture returns no result and callers do nothing.
sources: A: screenshot.rs:33-34 (Ok(None) on cancelled region capture, Esc / empty selection); screenshot.rs:60-64 (if the file does not exist after screencapture, return Ok(None); this check is not gated on mode).

B: common-crate.md:106 (a cancelled region selection returns Ok(None); callers treat it as a silent no-op). Interactive-only scope is implied by region selection in the same sentence; no error or message is stated, consistent with silent no-op.
edge_cases: Any capture that exits successfully but writes no file returns Ok(None), not only interactive cancels.
features.notes: Only in B. Outside the storage area per critique; not marked wrong, so kept.
features.check_notes: B's exact result agrees with A. A's source check shows Ok(None) also returns for any successful exit with no file, in both modes, so the trigger and edge cases are broadened.

features.title: Other app's window is not refreshed by a database write alone
features.trigger: Changing data in one app (for example the tray capture) while the other app is open
features.context: Both apps running, sharing ~/.taskscape/taskscape.db
features.result: Changes written to SQLite are visible to the other app's next read. The other window does not update by itself. The tray's capture submit posts POST /refresh to the main app's port (MAIN_PORT 7420) (tray task.rs:44). POST /focus is used by the tray to bring up an already-running main window (tray lib.rs:63), not as a documented refresh alternative.
sources: A: main/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1046 ("/refresh" route), lib.rs:1053 ("/focus" route); common/src/lib.rs:27-28 (MAIN_PORT 7420, TRAY_PORT 7421); tray/src-tauri/src/task.rs:44 (tray posts /refresh to MAIN_PORT after a capture write); tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:63 (tray posts /focus to MAIN_PORT when main is already running).

B: CLAUDE.md Gotchas: data changes propagate by writing SQLite and POSTing /refresh (or /focus) to the other app's HTTP port. CLAUDE.md line 3: main :7420, tray :7421 (common-crate.md:9 names only the MAIN_PORT/TRAY_PORT constants, not the numbers). common-crate.md:83-84: each app serves the data API on its port; only main adds /refresh, /focus and /quit. The doc does not state the HTTP method for these routes outside CLAUDE.md.
features.notes: Proposed by the critic; closes the open question in the shared-data entry above.
features.check_notes: B's claim that the writing app may POST either /refresh or /focus as a general refresh mechanism is not supported by source: A shows the tray posts /refresh to the main port after a capture write, and posts /focus only to bring up an already-running main window. B's point that only main serves /refresh, /focus and /quit agrees with A. Source decides.
